title: Frobenius acts on roots of unity by the q-th power
statement:
Let $k_0$ be a finite field with $q$ elements, $q=p^a$ with $p$ prime, and $k$ an algebraic closure of $k_0$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]; let $\varphi_q\in\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)$, $z\mapsto z^q$, be the arithmetic Frobenius and $\gamma=\varphi_q^{-1}$ the geometric Frobenius [def-weil-frobenius-substitution]. Let $N\geq1$ be an integer prime to $p$ and $\mu_N(k)=\{\zeta\in k^\times:\zeta^N=1\}$. Then:

1. $\mu_N(k)$ is a cyclic group of order $N$, and every automorphism $\sigma$ of the field $k$ maps $\mu_N(k)$ to itself.
2. $\varphi_q(\zeta)=\zeta^q$ and $\gamma(\zeta)=\zeta^{q'}$ for every $\zeta\in\mu_N(k)$, where $q'\in\mathbf Z$ is any integer with $qq'\equiv1\pmod N$ (it exists since $\gcd(q,N)=1$).
3. Let $\ell\neq p$ be a prime and $T_\ell\mu(k)=\varprojlim_r\mu_{\ell^r}(k)$, the limit along the maps $\zeta\mapsto\zeta^\ell$. It is a free $\mathbf Z_\ell$-module of rank one [def-weil-l-adic-numbers] (written additively), $\varphi_q$ and $\gamma$ act on it componentwise, and $\varphi_q$ acts as multiplication by $q\in\mathbf Z_\ell^\times$ and $\gamma$ as multiplication by $q^{-1}\in\mathbf Z_\ell^\times$.

source.place: (2.2), p. 281: 'si k = F_q, la substitution de Frobenius phi : x -> x^q agit [sur Q_l(1)] par multiplication par q'; the geometric Frobenius F = phi^{-1}: literature/deligne-weil-II_PMIHES-1980-52.pdf, (1.1.7), pp. 150-151
